analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: AI Stress Deepens as 2-5Y Treasuries Catch a Safety Bid
key_insights: The Nasdaq fell 5.52% on Thursday. The Nikkei and Kospi were each down around 6% in Friday Asia trading as tech names saw further selling. South Korea waived rules requiring collateral worth 140% of margin loans to prevent forced selling.

At 0700 GMT Friday, E-mini S&P 500 futures were down 0.12% and Nasdaq futures were up 0.64%. The author questions how long that holds given early weakness in European markets. Europe avoided the brunt of Thursday's moves, and the concern is whether this becomes a broader rout.
JGB futures gapped higher at the open, up 125 ticks from Thursday's close at 128.29. US Treasuries continued to rise but stayed below Thursday's high of 107-16.
The SOFR strip was up as much as four ticks. The market-implied chance of a December Fed rate hike fell to 66% from 81% on Wednesday.

Asia-hours option flow on Friday included 50k Week 1 TY 107.50/108 call spreads bought for 10. The spreads expire Friday and carry a 26 delta, equivalent to about 13k TY futures. There was also a block buyer of 8,200 TUZ6. Much of Thursday's flow was in the 2-5y bucket.

Nonfarm payrolls are due Friday, but the author doubts they matter given the focus on equities. UBS US Economics raised its October forecast to +75k total payrolls, with private payrolls +75k and government flat. Market consensus is 70k. Initial and continuing claims look better than last week on net.

Thursday's largest SOFR option flow was a buyer of 35k SFRZ6 95.9375/96.0625/96.1875 call flies from 1.5 up to 2.25, positioned for the Fed to pass on a December hike. The author expects more Fed-on-hold positioning if equity moves continue.

The author says it is early to draw conclusions from the AI selloff. The Fed will weigh the wealth effect from falling US equities and the possible employment and inflation impact of any reversal in data-centre construction.
CME preliminary open interest Thursday: SFRU7 rose 5.24% and SFRZ7 fell 5.2%. Spread volume was heavy in SFRM7/Z7 and SFRZ7/Z8. TUZ6 open interest rose 1.31% and TYZ6 rose 1.44%.

The Richmond Fed's October survey of 376 firms found 31% had some involvement in data-centre construction. Of those, about 68% said it was less than 10% of revenue. Firms more closely tied to data-centre construction saw larger increases in costs, prices and wages, and those directly involved were more upbeat on hiring.

UBS's Rebecca Cheong expects retail investors could sell more Friday ahead of the weekend, but says they are close to capitulation given Thursday's flow reversal. She sees three capitulation signals triggered: excess sell flow at -$365bn (a record), UBS RMM flow buying the dip at the 68th percentile versus 3y after the largest selling episode since Covid, and a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 96%. She expects SPX could set a low on Monday.

Cheong estimates Risk Control, Leveraged ETFs and CTAs sold a combined $170-210bn. Risk Control may need to sell another $200-270bn over the next two days. After Monday she expects Risk Control and CTA sell-rebalancing flows to become much smaller.

Data-centre loan risk transfers are a watch item. Bloomberg reports ING has put a $500m portfolio of data-centre loans, including debt tied to Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne, up for sale via a bids-wanted-in-competition process. Banks have reportedly been seeking insurance on loan portfolios for two weeks.

The FT reports Blackstone is doubling lock-up periods for some Asian investors in its flagship retail private-equity fund. New Singapore and Hong Kong clients in the $29bn BXPE fund must hold for at least four years or pay a penalty fee. The author says nothing suggests this is AI-related, but it matters given private-credit exposure to the sector.

Reuters reported in October that private credit could be called on to finance about $1tn of AI compute build-out. The author notes that when investors need cash, the most liquid investments are normally sold first.

tension_points.bull_case: Rebecca Cheong sees three capitulation signals triggered (record excess sell flow, RMM dip-buying, VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%) and expects SPX could set a low on Monday as systematic selling fades.
tension_points.bear_case: Mechanical selling is not finished. Risk Control may need to sell another $200-270bn over two days, retail could sell more Friday, and European markets showed early weakness.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued selling beyond Monday would undercut the Monday-low call, since Cheong expects Risk Control and CTA sell flows to become much smaller after that day.
